newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals futures end up on weaker yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals futures end up on weaker yen.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended higher on Tuesday, reflecting the yen's falls against the dollar during the long weekend, traders said.
Japanese markets were closed on Monday for a holiday.
Platinum futures were seven to 20 yen higher, with the benchmark June 1998 contract up 18 yen at 1,375 yen per gram.
"Buying orders emerged from the opening. The yen's weaker tone encouraged players here to buy," a brokerage trader said.
Local traders said no Russian platinum had arrived so far, although they had received a notice from Russian metal export agency Almaz that the exports would be resumed this week.
"We have no choice but to wait for platinum shipments," a brokerage house trader said.
Palladium futures ended sharply higher. The July and the October rose by the daily 22 yen limit by the close, and benchmark June was up 15 yen at 550 yen per gram.
Although the Russian agency had resumed palladium exports to Japan, the Japanese market was still tight, traders said.

"We received several palladium shipments from Russia last week, and local end-users rushed to buy them at once. We need more shipments to ease the supply tightness," a trader at a major trade house said.
Gold futures ended three to 10 yen higher, with the benchmark June up six yen at 1,201 yen per gram.
Bullion was quoted $325.40/80 per ounce at 0800 GMT, compared with $325.30/80 in New York overnight and a 12-year low fix of $315.75 in London earlier this month.
Silver futures were steady to 4.0 yen higher. Benchmark June was up 1.8 yen at 163.3 yen per 10 grams.
